feedback: Written before this candidate races. Evidence: iteration 4 (y = 0.07 m, span ±0.03 m, footprint 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.11 m, score 364.1) improved the oval to 16/20 finishes, but s-bend and slalom stayed at 0/20 with line-loss 1.4 and 1.95 per run and max_error 0.063 to 0.064 m. Iteration 2 (span ±0.04 m) and iteration 3 (footprint 0.016 m) both reduced scores, so those levers are closed. Iteration 0 to 1 wheel_track narrowing was confounded with mass and sensor changes, so turn authority is not yet proven, but it is the only untested geometry lever. Decision rules for the next race: (a) If s-bend and slalom line-loss is 1.0 or below and max_error is under 0.06 m, and the oval holds at 16/20 or better, keep wheel_track 0.10 m. (b) If line-loss is still above 1.0 with max_error near 0.06 m and the oval holds, the next geometry step is wheel_track 0.09 m, one step at a time, and only if the oval stays at 16/20 or better. (c) If line-loss stays at 1.4 or more on the sharp tracks at 0.10 m, narrowing is not enough. The Integrator should then change the controller weights, not the geometry. (d) If the oval falls below about 14/20 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 with low max_error, return wheel_track to 0.11 m, because the oscillation is then a weight problem.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 4 geometry and narrow only wheel_track from 0.11 to 0.10 m. Evidence: iteration 4 showed forward position helped the oval but left s-bend and slalom at 1.4 to 1.95 line-loss per run, so turn authority is the untested lever.

If s-bend or slalom line-loss is still above 1.0 per run with max_error near 0.06 m and the oval holds at 16/20 or better, try wheel_track 0.09 m next, with all other geometry unchanged. Do not go further than 0.09 m. Evidence: the narrowing from 0.12 to 0.11 m in iteration 1 was confounded, so this is a single-step test.

Keep sensor y at 0.07 m, span at ±0.03 m, sensor_size at 0.012 m, mass 0.7 kg and wheel_radius 0.03 m. Evidence: iteration 4 showed y = 0.07 m helped the oval (13/20 to 16/20). Iterations 2 and 3 showed span and footprint changes hurt. Speed is not limiting, since the oval completes in about 1.82 s.
